Qt and FFmpeg runtime attribution

The macOS and Windows application packages use Qt 6.11.3 and its multimedia
plugin. Windows uses the FFmpeg runtime supplied by that SDK. macOS builds
ABI-compatible FFmpeg 7.1.5 from the pinned source with the upstream
VideoToolbox dropped-frame allocation fix:
https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/commit/04ff86d0355a58c3d02dbf562ccb708942a29435
The extradata initializer also releases its locally owned queue node when
hardware encoder creation fails, before the software encoder is selected.
The build options and exact patch are in CMakeLists.txt at the application's
source revision. That shared runtime is used by both SquadSpeak and Qt.

Linux Qt 6.10.2 builds bundle the ABI-matching Qt Multimedia shared library,
rebuilt from the checksum-pinned source with cmake/qt-wayland.patch. The patch
adapts upstream portal request routing and session cleanup, cancels pending
requests on stop, resets capture state on restart and avoids the portal probe's
dynamic D-Bus introspection allocation. When instrumented against a regular
Qt SDK, the module retains Qt's Clang sanitizer link policy (ASan is supplied
by the test executable):
https://github.com/qt/qtmultimedia/commit/d2ae2aa07b40
https://github.com/qt/qtmultimedia/commit/2ccfc1fcb857
Build options and source checksum are recorded in CMakeLists.txt. The source
archive is included in the release dependency sources. This library also
contains dr_wav (Copyright 2023 David Reid), under MIT-0; its license text is
in QT-SBOM/licenses/MIT-0.txt. The Qt sources retain their LGPL/GPL notices.

The same Linux build bundles an ABI-matching Qt Qml shared library rebuilt
from the checksum-pinned Qt Declarative 6.10.2 source. cmake/qt-qml-gc.patch
backports the upstream QML garbage-collector transition correction so a
deadline-expired incremental collection still initializes its mark stack:
https://github.com/qt/qtdeclarative/commit/cdbacb7ba78779fc1eecc05afae3a3a874623e6e
The exact source archive and checksum are recorded in
cmake/source_archives.json. This attribution records the source and patch;
runtime validation remains part of the release test gate.

Qt source and licensing:
https://www.qt.io/licensing/
https://www.qt.io/terms-conditions/
https://code.qt.io/cgit/qt/qtmultimedia.git/tree/

The macOS SDK provides these unmodified records, installed under QT-SBOM/.
They describe the original SDK, not the rebuilt macOS FFmpeg or Linux library:
- qtbase-6.11.3.spdx
- qtmultimedia-6.11.3.spdx
- qtdeclarative-6.11.3.spdx
- qtimageformats-6.11.3.spdx
- qtsvg-6.11.3.spdx
- qttranslations-6.11.3.spdx

The qtmultimedia SBOM identifies the bundled FFmpeg component with this
license expression:
LGPL-2.1-or-later AND BSD-3-Clause AND BSD-2-Clause AND BSD-Source-Code AND ISC AND MIT AND MPL-2.0

The same SBOM identifies the Qt multimedia modules as available under the
Qt commercial terms or the applicable LGPL/GPL terms. The recipient must use
the terms matching the Qt SDK license and build configuration. This compact
record is paired with the SDK SBOM; it is not a substitute for that SBOM or
for the applicable license texts.
